rules.answer_classes: 2xx success; 410 gone (disable_endpoint gone_410, delivery paused); 413 give_up not_retried_413; 429, or 503 with a usable Retry-After: rate_limited, standard; 400/401/403/404/405/415/422 rejected class; 3xx redirect_refused, standard; any other status http_error, standard; timeout/dns_error/connect_error/tls_error/ssrf_blocked/worker_lost standard. The class follows the LAST answer.
rules.jitter: permille = 800 + floor(u32 * 401 / 2^32), u32 = first 4 bytes big-endian of sha256(utf8(jitter_seed + ':' + next_attempt_number)); delay_ms = base_delay_s * permille. Production seeds with the delivery id, so a delivery's schedule is reproducible and deliveries that failed together spread out.
rules.retry_after: integer seconds or an HTTP-date, on 429 and 503 only; delay_ms = max(jittered delay, min(retry_after_s, 3600) * 1000); a 429 also sets rate_halved_until = now + 300 s
rules.max_attempts: after attempt n fails, give up with max_attempts when n >= max_attempts[class] (checked before max age)
rules.max_age: give up with max_age_exceeded when retry_at > created_at + max_age_s (time paused counts)
rules.time_base: delays count from the attempt's settled_at_ms
rules.health: attempts oldest first; worker_lost, superseded and test attempts are ignored; a success resets the consecutive-failure run. disable: last failure is 410 -> gone_410; the last 3 failures are ssrf_blocked -> unsafe_address; >= 10 consecutive failures whose first is >= 24 h before now -> failing. Failing state: >= 3 consecutive failures spanning >= 10 min (first to last). Slow lane: 20 latency samples with the 10th smallest > 5,000 ms, or >= 3 timeouts with at_ms >= now - 10 min; slow_until = now + 30 min.
